chapter: Army service and after the war
title: Taken off the bandstand for the draft at Kansas City
summary: Booked a year ahead, he kept missing draft papers until two men arrived at the Kansas City auditorium and took him to Leavenworth.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So, really, then, up until the time you went in the Army, you were doing pretty good.
Oh, yes, well, you see, we were booked. By the time I went in the service, we were booked pretty good. I think about almost a year in advance.

We were -- well, at the time, everything had jelled pretty good. And it jelled good. And it was no trouble -- we was booked about a year ahead. And that's what was so disappointing. What I was trying to do, I wanted to take

my physical either in New York or California. So every time I'd get around New York, I'd write them and tell them to send my papers. The papers would never show. Or the papers would show after I would leave New York.

So I didn't contact them for a long time, til after we got to the West Coast. When I realized I was going to the West Coast, I told them, send my papers because I'll be moving around and everything, and I want to get it over with. So my papers came in, I think, a couple of days after I left California. And so we were one-nighting all the way back to New York then. We was on our way back to New York.
So we stopped in Kansas and do one night in Kansas City. And that's where it happened. We were on the stand -- we had a crowd, I guess we had about 6,000 or 7,000 people in there that night.

The auditorium there. And we had 6,000 or 7,000 people there. So a couple of guys came in and told me, says, we've got some very important business we've got to talk to you about. Says, 'now, we've got to do this as quick as as can.' I says, okay, well, everything's fine, everything's fine.' I said, 'we'll play a set, after the set.'
So they were nice enough. They stayed around til we took intermission. So we took intermission. Said, 'Mr. McShann, we've got to get together with you, we have some papers and

things here.' I says, 'okay, okay.' And we had a guy we called Friday that was the valet. Friday, I says, 'get these gentlemen a drink. Fix them up there. Give them a good shot, give them a double. Right with you,' and so on.

They went on and took them a taste. So they came back and says, now, -- we was getting ready to go back on the stand. They said, 'Mr. McShann, we've got to take you to Leavenworth.' Said, 'thanks for the drink and everything, but we've got to take you to Leavenworth right now.'

I said, 'no, no, not now.' They says, 'yeah, we've got to.' They says, 'that's why we're here.' I says, 'well, wait a minute, look here, I've got to finish tonight. Let me get through tonight and then we'll go up after I finish the dance.' They said, 'well, truthfully, we can't do that because we told them we'd bring you in right away. We were supposed to have taken you in at 9:00.'
